messages:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up — we need a concrete plan to operationalize FP8 / INT8 / 4-bit precision profiles for serving. goal: ship a safe, observable defaults set for Hosted + Dedicated within the quarter.

maria: TL;DR of constraints: 1) minimal perf regressions on our eval suites, 2) fallbacks without user-visible errors, 3) cheap rollouts (canary + auto-fallback), 4) runtime kernel coverage across instance types.

kevin: I ran the calibration suite last night. FP8 (E4M3-like) looks great on base perplexity for most open-weight models — median delta <1% vs fp16. problems show up on long-context coherence and some safety prompts. INT8 with per-channel scales is stable but loses edge-case generative quality on sparse attention patterns.

kevin: Recommendation: default profile = int8 for embedding + kv-cache, fp8 for attention + mlp when hardware supports it. 4-bit only as opt-in with group-wise per-channel scales and offline calibration.

josh: Ops/runtime note: our current kernel selector chooses by model_family + device. need to extend to precision_profile and per-layer override. that implies: 1) new profile config in model manifest, 2) compile-time kernel combos cached, 3) runtime fallback path when kernel unavailable.

josh: Example config (idea):
```
precision_profiles:
  - name: low-cost-int8
    layers: embed=int8, kv=int8, attn=fp16, mlp=fp16
    fallback_order: [int8, fp16]
    calibrate: true
  - name: perf-fp8
    layers: embed=fp16, kv=fp8, attn=fp8, mlp=fp8
    fallback_order: [fp8, fp16]
    calibrate: false
```

anita: Two risk items: telemetry and determinism.
1) We must capture token-level diffs on a small, representative prompt set during canary. without that we won't detect small safety regressions.
2) Quantized kernels can be non-deterministic across CUDA drivers/SM versions; we need to document supported driver matrix and add runtime checks to force fp16 fallback if nondeterminism detected.

maria: +1 on telemetry. add a regression gate: if token-error-rate (TER) vs baseline > X% on canary, auto-skip profile and alert SRE/product.

kevin: For calibration: prefer offline per-model calibration using representative dataset. online per-customer calibration is expensive and risky. we should offer a customer opt-in: "calibrate-on-dataset" that ingests N prompts and produces scales stored with model metadata.

josh: Implementation plan:
- phase 1: profile proto in runtime, support int8 + fp8 on latest AMX/GPU types, compile kernel combos, add fallback hooks (2 weeks)
- phase 2: canary + telemetry, TER checks, calibrator tooling (3 weeks)
- phase 3: docs + console UI + per-customer opt-in (2 weeks)

anita: Also need rollout policy in Console: route traffic % to profile, show per-token cost and per-profile latency histograms. product will want an "auto-apply" suggestion once profile passes gates.

maria: Edge-case: decoder-only models with flash attention and grouped quantization — group size tuning matters a lot. kevin, can you add a short doc with per-layer sensitivity matrix (embed/attn/mlp/ln) by model family? that will drive defaults.

kevin: Will do. I'll attach numbers for Llama-family, Mistral, and Red-Open variants. expected: ln + embed are low-sensitivity; attention heads and final layer norm are high-sensitivity.

josh: Question: do we expose profiles as named resources customers can pin (e.g., redwood:perf-fp8) or only internal classifier that picks at runtime? I'm leaning to named profiles (versioned) so customers can pin for reproducibility.

maria: Named, versioned profiles please. also tie profile -> model-version mapping in rollback plan.

anita: Tests: add unit test to ensure numeric rollback works: when fallback to fp16, KV cache must remain binary-compatible (no corruption). add a small end-to-end that runs 100 short prompts and compares hash of decoded tokens to allowed divergence threshold.

deploy-bot: deploy-trigger: canary/profiles/prod -> started (profile=perf-fp8, 2% traffic).

maria: Nice. For owners: kevin = eval + sensitivity matrices. josh = runtime + kernel selector changes. anita = telemetry/gates + console UX requirements. I'll own rollout plan + docs.

kevin: I'll start calibration runs tonight and post results in this thread (short table).

josh: I'll open a runtime PR with a minimal selector and a feature flag. keep it behind ff until we finish gating.

anita: I'll draft the SERP for canary gating and add alerts in ops playbook.

maria: Ok let's reconvene in 48h. thanks folks :thumbsup:
